thread:
claire: Quick design review — noticed a few micro-copy and keyboard flow issues in the trace viewer export flow. putting them here so engineering + a11y can weigh in.

ravi: thanks Claire. can you list the ones you saw?

claire: sure — main ones: 1) export button text reads 'Download' and appears in the overflow menu. users told me they weren't sure what format they'd get. 2) when the export modal opens, focus is not trapped; tabbing jumps behind the modal. 3) the 'Include timestamps' checkbox label is long and wraps at narrow widths, pushing the CTA below.

emily: +1 on the ambiguous label. suggestion: 'Export trace (JSON)' as primary label and show a chevron menu for other formats: JSON / HAR / CSV.

ravi: for a11y and handoff — prefer two things: explicit format in label and an extra aria-description that mentions file size estimate and what gets included. thoughts?

claire: yes — proposed label: `Export trace — JSON` and an `aria-describedby` that points to a short line: 'Includes spans, stack frames, and correlation ids; gzipped'. keeps it short but helpful.

emily: also noticed the copy on the confirmation toast says 'Export started' which is fine, but screen readers don't announce the filename when download completes. can we add an SR-only live region update like 'Trace export complete: filename.json'?

tj: good catch. on the implementation side we can fire an `aria-live='polite'` message when the file is ready. need product to confirm exact phrasing for the toast.

claire: suggested toast: 'Export complete — trace-<id>.json (contains spans & timestamps)'. short and machine-readable.

ravi: regarding focus trap — modal should put focus on the primary CTA and restore focus to the originating menu item on close. also keyboard shortcut: can we add `E` when trace panel focused to quickly open export? not necessary but nice.

emily: watch conflicts with other shortcuts. if we add one, it should be discoverable in the keyboard help overlay.

claire: layout nit: 'Include timestamps' label wraps at 320px. options: shorten to 'Timestamps' with a tooltip, or make the checkbox a stacked control with a shorter label and secondary hint. Which do y'all prefer?

ravi: prefer 'Timestamps' + tooltip (or SR description) to avoid layout shifts. tooltip can show 'Include absolute timestamps and timezone info'.

tj: implementation note: tooltip must be keyboard accessible (focusable) and we should avoid relying only on hover.

emily: copy tweak for correlation id copy button — currently button reads 'Copy' next to the ID. propose 'Copy correlation id' for screen readers and show icon-only for visual. aria-label should be `Copy correlation id {{id}}` so SR users get context.

claire: +1. also reaction: :mag_right: we should add a small affordance to reveal the timestamp of each span inline on hover/focus instead of forcing export for quick checks.

ravi: that's a new feature but useful. could be a toggle in the trace toolbar: 'Show timestamps inline'. low-effort to wire up if we already have timestamps in the DOM.

tj: to summarize action items: 1) change export label to include format, 2) trap focus in modal and restore on close, 3) SR live region for completion with filename, 4) shorten 'Include timestamps' to 'Timestamps' + tooltip, 5) aria-label update for copy button. i'll open a small PR for the focus + live region bits.

claire: awesome. i'll update the Sketch and make a handoff note for the copy. emily, can you update the copy strings?

emily: yep — will put strings in the shared copy doc and add examples for toast messages, aria-labels, and tooltip text.

ravi: i'll run a quick a11y pass on the PR once it's up and test with NVDA/VoiceOver.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: New branch opened: feature/trace-export-accessibility by tj — build queued. :rocket:

claire: thanks everyone. will follow up with the updated assets and a tiny UX spec for the keyboard flow.

emily: added a todo for me in the copy doc: update string keys and add test cases for screen reader announcements.

tj: PR link (when ready) in #eng-runtime and ping @ravi @claire for review.

claire: end.
